name: PaaS platform
title:
PaaS
platform
summary: A service management interface and infrastructure automation, developed collaboratively.

chapters.label: CONTEXT
chapters.title:
A platform
for services
chapters.text: The project started without existing infrastructure or DevOps processes. The team needed a platform to deploy and operate applications: a user interface, backend services and a runtime environment.

chapters.label: MY CONTRIBUTION
chapters.title:
Frontend
and automation
chapters.text: Built the frontend with Next.js and TypeScript and coordinated frontend development. Wrote scripts for cloud operations and backend infrastructure. DevOps was a shared responsibility; my colleagues developed and led the backend.

chapters.label: TECHNOLOGY
chapters.title:
Code
and environments
chapters.text: The platform used Kubernetes, Argo CD, Terraform and Ansible. The frontend used Next.js with SSR; the team’s backend used FastAPI and Celery. My infrastructure contribution focused on automating cloud and environment operations.

chapters.label: OUTCOME
chapters.title:
Interface
and tooling
chapters.text: Delivered the platform frontend and scripts for cloud operations and backend infrastructure. The team’s shared infrastructure provided a repeatable delivery process through CI/CD and GitOps.

name: Kubernetes & CI/CD
title:
Kubernetes
and operations
summary: Automated configuration and more reliable services for a commercial system.

chapters.label: BEFORE
chapters.title:
Manual work
and outages
chapters.text: Configuration changes were applied manually. Infrastructure and service operations needed to become easier to manage. Sentry also suffered recurring outages: backups blocked disk access and Snuba consumers crashed.

chapters.label: MY CONTRIBUTION
chapters.title:
Configuration
as code
chapters.text: Automated infrastructure and service configuration with IaC, including e-commerce and Grafana. For e-commerce, replaced manual configuration rollout with a GitLab-triggered workflow. Maintained Kubernetes, Helm, CI/CD and the existing Harbor registry.

chapters.label: OPERATIONS
chapters.title:
Reliable
Sentry operation
chapters.text: Traced Snuba consumer crashes to backups and disk blocking. Configured restarts, monitoring and Grafana alerts. Also worked with ELK, Vault and LDAP for logging, secrets and access management.

chapters.label: OUTCOME
chapters.title:
Faster changes.
Fewer outages.
chapters.text: E-commerce configuration rollout became faster: a GitLab action replaced manual steps. Sentry now operates reliably and the recurring outages no longer interrupt developers. Infrastructure and service configuration is automated through IaC.

name: Developer platform
title:
Developer
platform
summary: Shared build, delivery and code-quality workflows for teams using different stacks.

chapters.label: CONTEXT
chapters.title:
Different stacks.
Shared workflows.
chapters.text: Several teams used different technology stacks without a consistent approach to delivery and operations. Build, deployment and onboarding workflows needed to be standardized.

chapters.label: MY CONTRIBUTION
chapters.title:
Repeatable
delivery
chapters.text: Built and maintained GitLab CI and Jenkins pipelines. Worked on shared Helm chart standards, common logging and monitoring tools, and infrastructure documentation.

chapters.label: AUTOMATION
chapters.title:
Code quality
checks
chapters.text: Deployed and maintained SonarQube. Automated project synchronization through the GitLab and SonarQube APIs, connecting team projects to a shared quality-checking system.

chapters.label: OUTCOME
chapters.title:
Easier service
onboarding
chapters.text: Shared pipelines and deployment standards simplified project onboarding. SonarQube synchronization is automated. Teams have a consistent delivery process and common diagnostic tools.

name: Anti-DDoS & resilience
title:
Anti-DDoS
and resilience
summary: Automated interaction with protection services and fewer manual steps during incidents.

chapters.label: CONTEXT
chapters.title:
Responding
to network attacks
chapters.text: A production system faced network attacks. Incident response needed fewer manual operations and a clear sequence of actions.

chapters.label: MY CONTRIBUTION
chapters.title:
Protection
through APIs
chapters.text: Automated interaction with StormWall and Qrator Labs anti-DDoS services, moving protection-service operations into scripts.

chapters.label: OPERATIONS
chapters.title:
Monitoring
and response
chapters.text: Configured monitoring and alerts and documented response procedures, connecting problem detection to specific engineering actions.

chapters.label: OUTCOME
chapters.title:
Less
manual work
chapters.text: Automation reduced manual interaction with protection services and the engineering workload during attacks. Documented procedures made incident response more predictable.

name: AI
title:
LLM
security
summary: Language-model protection and LoRA adapter verification. Dissertation research with a software prototype and experiments.

chapters.label: CONTEXT
chapters.title:
Language-model
resilience
chapters.text: When an LLM reads external content or calls tools, manipulated input can change its behavior. My dissertation investigates resilience to adversarial attacks and verification of third-party LoRA adapters.

chapters.label: MY CONTRIBUTION
chapters.title:
A VRF + LoRA
prototype
chapters.text: Developed a session-dependent LoRA parameter-shift method and its software implementation: verifiable shift generation, attack simulation, inference auditing and quality measurement. Built the testbed with Python, PyTorch, Transformers and PEFT.

details.title: Implementation details
details.text: The prototype derives a verifiable shift using Ed25519 and SHAKE-256. The inference server and auditor can run in separate processes: the auditor reproduces the shift on a reference model and compares logits. The protection module is registered as software under No. 2025665020.

chapters.label: RESULTS
chapters.title:
Experimental
results
chapters.text: Evaluated GCG on TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat using 10 AdvBench prompts. The shift increased attack loss under the same optimization budget. Transferred suffixes failed; direct optimization against the shifted model also produced no successful attacks in this sample.

details.title: Test conditions and limitations
details.text: Success was defined by a target affirmative phrase at the beginning of the response. Sample: 10 AdvBench prompts; LoRA r=8; shift amplitude 0.1. On 8 MT-Bench questions, long-answer diversity decreased (distinct-2: 0.91 → 0.62), so amplitude requires tuning. Auditor verification averaged 0.772 s on TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat, Apple MPS, across 10 control queries. These findings apply to the described testbed and do not establish universal protection against prompt injection.

chapters.label: APPLICATION
chapters.title:
Assessing
AI-system risks
chapters.text: Practical follow-up work includes pilot LLM robustness assessments, reproducible evaluation testbeds and inference-component verification. Teams can assess protection, response quality and computational costs before integrating a method into a product.
chapters.note: A research foundation for applied AI work

details.title: Scope of application
details.text: The approach requires access to model weights and the LoRA adapter. The dissertation recommends standardized ECVRF for industrial use instead of the experimental scheme. Small logit perturbations may remain undetected at the chosen threshold. Natural-language prompt injections require additional detection mechanisms and restrictions on agent permissions.
